policy.last_change: 4 Mar 2026 (-25bp, eff. 5 Mar); held 9 Apr, 6 May and 2 Jun

policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 18 Jun close (1x4 3.85, 3x6 3.87, 6x9 3.96, 9x12 4.06 vs WIBOR 3M 3.84) price roughly 20bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 2 Jun (May CPI eased mainly on food; decisions stay data-dependent); Glapiński (3 Jun): lower May CPI cuts the hike odds, rates are high enough and there is no reason to change or even discuss them. Duda (18 Jun): stable rates the base case, little room for cuts; the May voting record (18 Jun) shows Tyrowicz's +100bp motion rejected again. May CPI 3.1% (final, 15 Jun; flash 29 May, 3.7% expected); core 3.1% (16 Jun). Standard fuel excise is back from 15 Jun; VAT 8% and price caps run to 30 June, with a VAT decision due 'shortly' (Tusk, 16 Jun).
policy.risk_text: Strong demand at the 17 Jun sale (cover 1.52) and a dovish MPC pulled the 10Y to ~5.40%; risks: the hawkish Fed dots lifted US 2Y yields, CPI may rise as fuel support is withdrawn (VAT after 30 Jun), and the US-Iran MoU is fragile; one more sale on 24 Jun.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%; EC (21 May): GDP 3.5% in 2026; OECD (June outlook): CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027; Fitch (8 Jun): GDP 3.3%, NBP flat at 3.75% to year-end; World Bank (11 Jun): GDP 3.1% / 2.6%. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after May PLN 108.2bn (~40% of the limit, 15 Jun); the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; EC (21 May): 6.5%, debt 64.5%; EKF consensus (2 Jun): 6.9%; EDP debt 61.6% of GDP at end-Q1 (10 Jun); 2027 budget path (9 Jun): GDP 3.1%, CPI 2.5%; the government adopted the windfall tax (16 Jun); fuel package (VAT 8%, price caps) to 30 June, standard excise back from 15 June.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~58-59% (after 17 Jun, banks) financed; budget accounts PLN 208.3bn at end-May (MoF, 8 Jun); 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%; BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds (2 Jun). S&P A-/stable (affirmed 8 May); Scope A negative (15 May); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks; Fitch's June forecast round (8 Jun) was not a rating action.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun; May CPI 3.1% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (second estimate). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 18 Jun: MPC's Duda: stable rates the base case, little room for cuts. May voting record: Tyrowicz's +100bp motion rejected again. GUS: June consumer confidence up (BWUK -9.9); price expectations 20.2 from 24.7. BGK switch: sold FPC 1.35bn, bought back FPC0427 1.44bn. Banks: 2026 needs 58-59% financed; the 17 Jun additional sale added PLN 0.79bn. After the hawkish Fed (dots) SPW rose 5-7bp (PAP); DS0436 5.44%. Abroad: the BoE held 7-2 (Greene, Pill for a hike), the CNB hiked to 3.75% (6-1), SNB and Norges held (Norges signals a hike). The US-Iran MoU took effect after Trump and Pezeshkian signed; Khamenei approved it and tankers crossed Hormuz; Brent ~$77-80, gold -3%. EUR/USD below 1.15, DXY at a one-year high; FedWatch ~50% for a September hike. UK unemployment fell to 4.9%; Philly Fed 10.3.

calendar.plan_text: MoF June plan (29 May): one switch on 3 Jun (settles 8 Jun; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527) and sale auctions on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each) in OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed. 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%. 17 Jun sale: PLN 12.00bn vs 18.27bn demand (cover 1.52) plus 0.79bn; OK0129 4.399%, PS0731 4.918%, DS1030 4.711%, DS0436 5.416%. BGK switch (18 Jun): PLN 1.35bn of FPC sold (demand 2.11bn) vs 1.44bn of FPC0427 bought back.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining June operations: 24 Jun. Next MPC in July, with the NBP projection: a hold is expected. Covers: 1.52 (17 Jun) vs 1.25-1.33 in May.

facts.core_text: Regime: the US-Iran MoU in force - Brent below $80, hawkish Fed dots, a CNB hike; the NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun while FRAs price roughly 20bp of NBP hikes; the ECB hiked to 2.25% on 11 Jun with one more hike priced, the Fed signals a 2026 hike in its dots, the BoE held 7-2, the CNB hiked to 3.75% and the MNB is on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 50bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 255bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 18 Jun close). BoE 7-2 hold; CNB hikes to 3.75% (18 Jun).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK's first FPC switch (18 Jun): PLN 1.35bn sold (demand 2.11bn) vs 1.44bn of FPC0427 bought back (net about -0.09bn); Q3 issuance to prefund 2027 needs.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
